P001.text: Act on a proposed linked history for each sampled first order, its fulfillment, the product or container received, and any subsequent refill attempt or second order.

P002.text: The target counterpart of custody is the documented passage of that particular order and product through service handlers and customer handling, together with the provenance of evidence about those events.

P003.text: Whether existing records permit reliable customer and order linkage is unknown and must be checked.

P004.text: Nonpurchase at eight weeks is an outcome requiring explanation, not an identified break in handling or evidence of dissatisfaction.

P005.text: During week one, check linkage and compare cohorts with a full eight weeks of observation, using consistent definitions of first and second orders.

P006.text: Examine differences in quantity, product, discount and fulfillment; establish starter-container status only where records or customers support it.

P007.text: Select a limited follow-up sample spanning purchasers and nonpurchasers, promotion exposure and fulfillment routes, including the new collection points.

P008.text: Invite voluntary participation without repeated unsolicited contact.

P009.text: For consenting participants, reconstruct the particular order's history from ordering through dispatch, delivery or collection, receipt, storage, use and any refill attempt.

P010.text: For each documented transfer or handling event, record the responsible actor or reporting source, time or explicitly uncertain interval, purpose, order/product/container linkage, and supporting evidence.

P011.text: Ask about remaining stock, expected depletion, leaks, collection access and refill understanding without presuming a cause.

P012.text: Distinguish existing records, customer recollections and unresolved discrepancies.

P013.text: Trace each finding back to its source; retain corrections and restrict access to identifiable histories.

P014.text: Seek clarification only within agreed follow-up, and leave unresolved links marked as gaps.

P015.text: By the end of week one, choose at most one reversible fulfillment or communication change addressing a corroborated, traceable difficulty.

P016.text: For example, trial revised refill instructions only if histories connect confusing instructions with failed or abandoned refill attempts.

P017.text: Run the change for the remaining four weeks; if feasible, randomly assign eligible consenting customers to changed or usual communication and document assignment and actual receipt.

P018.text: If evidence does not identify an actionable process within this scope, make no speculative process change.

P019.text: Look for continuous, internally consistent histories linking the order, the received product, the relevant service encounters and the evidence examined.

P020.text: Corroboration might connect dispatch and collection records with a participant's account of receiving the same order; contradictions might concern receipt dates, quantities or which purchase supplied the product discussed.

P021.text: A missing use history remains a documentation gap.

P022.text: Separately record reported stock remaining, anticipated refill timing, specific difficulties and refill attempts, with their source and uncertainty.

P023.text: During a trial, document whether the changed process reached the intended customer, whether the identified step was completed, and any subsequent order.

P024.text: These are proposed observations, not established findings.

P025.text: Documentary continuity supports attributing an examined experience or trial exposure to the intended first order and accounts for its documented handling history.

P026.text: This makes particular explanations more discriminating: reliably linked remaining stock can support delayed need for that household; a documented unsuccessful collection or refill attempt can support a particular inconvenience.

P027.text: Neither establishes how much of the overall decline that explanation accounts for.

P028.text: Gaps weaken attribution and call for clarification or exclusion from conclusions requiring that link, rather than classification as dissatisfaction.

P029.text: At week five, use verified trial exposure, completion of the affected step, participant accounts and operational burden to decide whether to retain or revert the single change.

P030.text: A credible randomized comparison can strengthen a narrow causal claim about the measured step.

P031.text: Keep the purchasing commitment provisional with respect to any claimed repeat-purchase uplift: calculate scenarios from observed orders and explicitly uncertain future refill demand.

P032.text: A complete history does not prove truthful reporting, accurate recall or absence of unrecorded events; a gap does not prove a service failure or product alteration.

P033.text: Reliability depends on identifier quality, recording practices, preservation of sources and safeguards against mistaken linkage.

P034.text: Voluntary participants and support correspondents may differ from silent customers, so their explanation frequencies do not estimate population prevalence.

P035.text: Promotions and collection-point openings coincided, preventing a simple before-and-after attribution.

P036.text: Quantity purchased does not establish consumption speed.

P037.text: Four weeks of trial follow-up cannot establish an eight-week repeat-purchase effect for new trial entrants.

P038.text: Stop individual follow-up on withdrawal; suspend the trial for credible increased harm or service disruption.

P039.text: If exposure, identity or outcome linkage cannot be established, do not infer an effect from those cases.

P040.text: At five weeks, report unresolved explanations and base purchasing on explicit demand scenarios rather than an assumed recovery; assess mature repeat-order outcomes later using routine records, with further contact only by agreement.
